duplicate_groups.condition_differences: None: the same always-on language rule in the language contract and in both harness always-on bodies.
duplicate_groups.rationale: The always-on essentials are duplicated on purpose: a rule deployed as a skill is not loaded unbidden, so the language rule is repeated in the two bodies every session reads (rules/workflow-globals.md:29-33; ADR-0003 Decision 2). The naming migration moves both bodies with their text unchanged except stale names (spec 09 REQ-55).

duplicate_groups.condition_differences: None: the commit-message and attribution rule of the git-flow contract, repeated in both always-on bodies.
duplicate_groups.rationale: The commit rule must hold in sessions that load no git-flow skill, so the always-on essentials carry it (rules/workflow-globals.md:29-33; ADR-0003 Decision 2); the contract stays the canonical text (rules/git-flow.md:86).

duplicate_groups.condition_differences: None: the same search policy in the two harness always-on bodies.
duplicate_groups.rationale: Both always-on bodies carry the same essentials by ADR-0003 Decision 2. The machine-specific lines inside this policy are recorded separately by AUD-08-022 and AUD-08-023; the duplication itself is the decided form.

duplicate_groups.condition_differences: rules/phase-atomic-execution.md states the reuse condition, path resolution and load order for atomic execution (loaded by /phase-atomic-execution, /pae-tests and /pae-implement); rules/phase-atomic-validation.md states them for atomic validation (loaded by /phase-atomic-validation and /pav-check).
duplicate_groups.rationale: Each bootstrap is loaded alone at the start of its phase, so each must hold its own reuse condition and Step 0 before anything else is loaded; the naming migration keeps one bootstrap rule per phase (spec 09 REQ-18, REQ-19). The repeated path resolution weighs on the size of the atomic-execution bootstrap (AUD-08-063).

duplicate_groups.condition_differences: Each phase rule lists its own sources under the same table header, and the three orchestrator-phase rules state the same umbrella order for their own phase.
duplicate_groups.rationale: The shared header and umbrella sentence are the common shape of the five bootstrap rules, each loaded only for its phase; the naming migration keeps that shape (spec 09 REQ-19).

duplicate_groups.condition_differences: None: the same obligation for the same step; the workflow adds that missing tooling never justifies level `none` (workflows/pae-tests.md:64-65).
duplicate_groups.rationale: /pae-tests applies the phase behaviour at the step where it captures the test command; the rule states it for every atomic-execution step. One sentence, kept where it is acted on.

duplicate_groups.condition_differences: None: the quick path applies the RED criterion of the tdd rule, which it cites (rules/quick-flow.md:86).
duplicate_groups.rationale: The quick path's numbered TDD steps restate the one sentence that defines RED so the step is complete where it is executed; the tdd rule stays canonical.

duplicate_groups.condition_differences: None: two different tables in the same section share a column header (rules/run-log.md:205, :254).
duplicate_groups.rationale: Only the header row repeats; the table bodies differ, so nothing is stated twice.

duplicate_groups.condition_differences: None: the same vocabulary for the same fields; the `atomic-tests` line that follows differs in wording, not in values (rules/workflow-globals.md:217, rules/workflow-reference.md:227).
duplicate_groups.rationale: The anchored status line has one canonical place; the copy in rules/workflow-reference.md is read by no check (AUD-08-060). The naming migration keeps every parent line starting `Status values for` (spec 09 AC-42), so the consolidation follows it and no map decision performs it (A-20: owner 11).

duplicate_groups.condition_differences: Each atomic workflow resolves its own argument and locates and checks its own progress block before acting; the stop messages name each workflow's phase.
duplicate_groups.rationale: Every one of these workflows has an `Invocation:` line and may run standalone, so each validates its own input; the lines are guards, not shared definitions.

duplicate_groups.condition_differences: Each phase workflow takes its task directory and stops on its own phase status; the stop messages name the phase.
duplicate_groups.rationale: Standalone-invocable steps each check their own argument and phase state before acting; the repetition is the guard of each entry point.

duplicate_groups.condition_differences: Each workflow loads the bootstrap rule of its own phase (atomic execution, atomic validation, discovery or validation) at its own entry.
duplicate_groups.rationale: A step invoked standalone must load its phase rule; the general load order and reuse sentences are rules/workflow-globals.md:35-37. The repeated loads under a parent are recorded as load-repeat findings (AUD-08-051, AUD-08-052, AUD-08-053), not as duplicated text.

duplicate_groups.condition_differences: The workflows resolve the description and parent paths before changing directories and name the base of a relative `working_dir:` (the atomic task directory, workflows/pav-check.md:28-30); the rule's Step 0 states the result for any caller (rules/phase-atomic-execution.md:16-20).
duplicate_groups.rationale: The workflow must resolve its paths before it can load the rule from the resolved knowledge base; the statements agree on reading.

duplicate_groups.condition_differences: /pae-implement reads the design constraints before writing code; /pav-check reads them to check the implementation against them.
duplicate_groups.rationale: Two steps read the same inputs for different decisions; each line is the step's own input list.

duplicate_groups.condition_differences: Each orchestrator opens or inherits its own run and logs its own boundaries (/phase-execution, /phase-validation, /phase-discovery, /phase-pipeline, /spec-run).
duplicate_groups.rationale: Run ownership is decided per orchestrator; the shared sentences apply the routing section to each. The full-rule load behind them is AUD-08-039.

duplicate_groups.condition_differences: /phase-pipeline passes the phase to its children in the autonomous pipeline; /spec-run passes it to its sub-agents in orchestrated mode.
duplicate_groups.rationale: The two orchestrators pass the same argument in different run modes.

duplicate_groups.condition_differences: None: /suggest-pr-description reuses the context step of /suggest-commit-message and states the same stop.
duplicate_groups.rationale: The PR description workflow cites the commit-message step as its definition and restates only the stop it relies on.

duplicate_groups.condition_differences: /phase-atomic-execution reuses a caller's resolution only for the same invocation (workflows/phase-atomic-execution.md:97-98); /spec-run stops its setup when guidance is unavailable and never implements inline (workflows/spec-run.md:186, :203), the caller's own conservative path that the contract leaves to it (rules/workflow-reference.md:124-125).
duplicate_groups.rationale: Read-detected: three workflows paraphrase the model-resolution contract in about twenty lines each; no paraphrase contradicts it, and the caller-specific parts are short. No map decision performs the consolidation (A-20: owner 11).

statements.text: - Use `.ai/memory/architecture.md` to scope source reads. Read affected source when verifying behavior, freshness, or a concrete pattern; an inventory description alone is not implementation evidence.
- Budget: max 12 files (8 entry-points + 4 one-level-deeper). Hard limit.
- Document every file read with reason: "read to verify <specific behavior or gap>."
- Stop reading when affected parts are understood.
Discovery runs **autonomously by default**; `--step-by-step` switches it to manual review. See `/phase-discovery → ## Execution Modes` (the workflow, not this rules file).

- Task requirements unclear → resolve by research in this order: `.ai/principles/*` → `.ai/adr/` → `.ai/memory/*` → existing codebase patterns → general best practice. Record the resolution in `## Task Analysis → ### Assumptions`. Never infer intent silently — inferring is allowed, hiding it is not.
- Decomposition boundary or architectural choice ambiguous → generate 2–3 options and resolve them with `workflow-reference → ## Autonomous Decision Protocol`. Record the scoring and rationale.
- Steps 1→4 run back-to-back. A step's completion report is not a handoff.
- Stop only on the Autonomous Decision Protocol's escalation conditions or a Guard confirmation that would overwrite existing artifacts.
- Task requirements unclear → ask before proceeding. Never infer intent silently.
- Decomposition boundary ambiguous → present 2–3 options with trade-offs, wait for decision.
- Architectural variants → present, wait for the user's choice.
- After each of Steps 1–4 → stop and wait for review.

findings.section: ## Recorded state — required for resume and for restack
findings.observation: Two section references omit the `##` marker of their target heading: `workflow-globals → Canonical Status Formats` and `workflow-reference → Protected Sections Contract`. Both targets exist as level-2 headings, so a reader finds them, but the cross-reference syntax requires the marker and the naming migration's executable-reference grammar does not read the unmarked form.
findings.consequence: No grammar-based check or rewrite sees these references, so a renamed or split target leaves them stale without a diagnostic.
findings.closure: Both spans carry the marker of the target heading (`## Canonical Status Formats`, `## Protected Sections Contract`); the naming migration fixes them under AMD-08-01.

findings.observation: `phase-atomic-execution → ## Context Bootstrap` names a stem that is both a rule and a workflow, and both files have a `## Context Bootstrap` heading. The intended target is the rule, whose bootstrap holds the runbook resolution with the umbrella fallback.
findings.consequence: A reader or tool cannot tell from the reference which file is meant; the shared stem resolves only by reading the surrounding prose.
findings.closure: The reference names a stem that is unique after the naming migration (the rule's new bootstrap name).

findings.observation: `/phase-discovery → ## Execution Modes` names a stem shared by the rule and the workflow. Only the workflow has the heading, and the prose adds "the workflow, not this rules file" to disambiguate.
findings.consequence: The reference depends on a prose note to resolve; the rule-side candidate is a missing heading.
findings.closure: The reference names the workflow by a stem that no rule shares after the naming migration.

findings.observation: Lines 21 and 22 cite `workflow-globals → Never auto-advance between phases` and `workflow-globals → Test-first execution`; neither is a heading of rules/workflow-globals.md, both are bold paragraph labels inside its `## Context Pack` section (:56, :114). Lines 125-126 split `workflow-globals → Canonical Status Formats` across a line break, so no span forms and no tool reads it.
findings.consequence: The references cannot be resolved or loaded as sections, and the split one escapes every reference check.
findings.closure: Each reference names an existing heading in the marked form on one line: the cited paragraph's own heading once AUD-08-026 gives it one, otherwise `## Context Pack`, whose extent holds both paragraphs; the naming migration fixes them under AMD-08-01.

findings.observation: Two section references omit the `##` marker: `workflow-globals → Canonical Status Formats` (:35) and `quick-flow → The quick path` (:201), the second also a bare prefix of the heading `## The quick path — what changes`.
findings.consequence: The references escape grammar-based checks and rewriting; with the marker added, the second would resolve only through the accepted ` — ` prefix form.
findings.closure: Both spans carry the marker of the target heading (`## Canonical Status Formats`, `## The quick path — what changes`); the naming migration fixes them under AMD-08-01.

findings.observation: The span `.ai/context-pack.md` names the pack file a consumer project generates, not workflows/context-pack.md; the md-name match on its last path component resolves to the workflow and sets the md suffix flag. Read in context the text is correct and needs no change. The same match occurs in docs/USAGE.md:803 and .ai/principles/domain.md:49, where the span `.ai/context-pack.md` also names the generated pack file.
findings.consequence: None for the instruction; the edge and its load entry are detection artifacts.
findings.closure: No change; the edge stays recorded as correct on reading.

findings.observation: `quick-flow →` and `## Mid-flight escalation` are split across a line break, so no span forms. Joined, the reference would still not resolve: the heading is `## Mid-flight escalation (quick → full)`, a parenthesised suffix the heading grammar does not accept, and its text contains ` → `, which a section reference cannot cite.
findings.consequence: No reader or check sees the reference, and the target heading cannot be cited in the cross-reference syntax as written.
findings.closure: The reference sits on one line as one span that names `## Mid-flight escalation (quick → full)` with its marker; no heading is renamed; the naming migration fixes it under AMD-08-01.

findings.observation: The file holds a bootstrap (`## Context Bootstrap`, `## Phase Behaviors`, :8-51) and a procedure triggered by `atomic-execution: blocked` on entry (`## Blocker Reconciliation`, :53-71). The reading agrees with the naming migration's section map, which moves the procedure to its own rule.
findings.consequence: Every caller of the bootstrap loads the reconciliation procedure even when no subtask is blocked.
findings.closure: The section map's split of this file is carried out, or amended with a recorded reason.

findings.observation: The file holds a bootstrap (`## Context Bootstrap`, :8-34) and two conduct sections: `## Codebase Reading Rules` (:36-41: scope, budget, record and stop criteria for reading) and `## Decision Protocol` (:43-64: how ambiguities are resolved in each mode). The reading agrees with the naming migration's section map (bootstrap and discovery conduct protocol).
findings.consequence: The conduct rules load with the bootstrap list although they apply at decision points later in Discovery.
findings.closure: The section map's split is carried out, or amended with a recorded reason; the statement coverage of the two conduct sections decides whether the autonomous decision protocol can receive them.

findings.section: ## Worked example A — rejected by the gate (export pipeline changes)
findings.observation: The always-on contract carries two worked examples (:156-202) and a pointer to an incident that the file does not explain (:39-40, repeated in rules/workflow-globals.md:140-141). Both explain rather than oblige; the gate (:27-57), the quick path (:61-114) and the escalation (:137-152) stay reachable without them.
findings.consequence: Every session that loads the rule reads the examples, and the incident pointer cannot be followed from the rule.
findings.closure: The worked examples move to a reference file that is not loaded by default, and the incident pointer is either explained or removed from the contract text.

findings.observation: The contract holds a decision protocol (`## Test-level gate`, :54-82), a procedure triggered by behaviour-preserving work (`### The procedure`, :132-151) and a rationale section (`## Why the order matters`, :219-226). The gate and the procedure are invoked from `/pae-tests` and from the quick path, so they stay with the contract; the rationale is short.
findings.consequence: The target name `contract-tdd` will hold sections of three other kinds.
findings.closure: The map records the kept sections under the contract with a reason, or splits the gate and procedure through an amendment.

findings.observation: The contract holds the three-call logging procedure every pipeline follows (`## How a pipeline logs`, :58-112) and a decision table for each checkpoint boundary (`## Workflow coverage and routing`, :116-184).
findings.consequence: The target name `contract-run-log` will hold a procedure and a protocol section.
findings.closure: The map keeps the sections in the contract with a recorded reason, or splits them through an amendment.

findings.observation: The always-on rule carries the internal contracts of the helper and the hook adapter: argument validation and writes (:280-302), correlated interval arithmetic (:304-373), native transcript parsing and private ownership states (:375-521) and lint output (:523-560). They bind scripts/log-step.sh and hooks/log-step-hook.sh; the workflow agent acts on the three calls (:58-112) and the routing table (:116-184), and the adapter part applies only where a capability record declares `hooks: yes`.
findings.consequence: Every session that loads the rule reads implementation detail it cannot act on, including a harness-specific session variable (:393) on harnesses without hooks.
findings.closure: The helper and adapter internals are classified as reference or conditional context, loaded only for work on the helper or where hooks are declared, and the agent-facing calls and routing table stay in the always-loaded contract.

findings.observation: The always-on contract embeds a decision protocol among cross-workflow obligations inside `## Context Pack` ("Wait for user decisions", :60, and the trust mechanism, :98-102) and an environment lookup in the preamble (rule resolution per harness, :19-33).
findings.consequence: The protocol parts have no heading of their own, so they cannot be cited or loaded as sections.
findings.closure: The map records where the embedded protocol and lookup go, with headings that can be cited, or keeps them with a recorded reason.

findings.observation: The preamble instructs how a rule reference resolves on Windsurf and Devin (rules directories and bare basenames) next to the skill resolution of the two current harnesses; the mentions are active behaviour, not history.
findings.consequence: The contract keeps a resolution path for environments the naming migration retires.
findings.closure: The Windsurf and Devin resolution is removed or marked historical when the naming migration retires those environments.

findings.observation: The rule-resolution instruction chooses between a bare basename and the `rule-` skill prefix by harness name ("On Claude Code and Codex", "on Windsurf and Devin") rather than by a declared capability such as rules delivered as skills.
findings.consequence: A further harness has no defined resolution until the text names it.
findings.closure: The resolution is stated by capability, with the harness facts in the capability records.

findings.observation: Besides contracts and the two decision protocols that the section map already separates, the file holds a procedure (`## Description Amendment`, :66-91; the composite promotion steps inside the classifier, :530-544) and reference material (`## Legacy tasks`, :584-586, which names one consumer's old directories; `## File Location Reference`, :619-634).
findings.consequence: The target `contract-state-files` will hold a procedure and reference sections that are not needed to act.
findings.closure: The map records where the procedure and reference sections go, or keeps them with a recorded reason.

findings.observation: Lines 346-373 (composite protected lines, protected `plan.md` items and protected fields) continue the list of `## Protected Sections Contract` (:280-323) but sit under `## Multi-Phase Spec Rules` (:325), after a rule line at :344. `## Reference Tables (moved from workflow-globals)` (:259) is an empty section followed directly by `## Status Translation Table` (:261).

findings.observation: The contract of roles and shared files ends with a decision protocol: class A and class B routing and the conditions that always stop the run (:137-191). It is cohesive with the roles it routes between.
findings.consequence: The target name `contract-orchestration` will hold a protocol section.

findings.observation: Lines 20-21 are written as comments but are Markdown level-1 headings, and :21 points to one harness's personal instruction file in a rule deployed to every harness.
findings.consequence: Every harness reads a heading that is not a heading and an instruction that names only one harness's file.

findings.observation: The always-on body names one host ("On this Linux host") and gives two absolute home-directory paths of one machine for the ast-grep program and its configuration. The file is copied as the global instructions of every installation.
findings.consequence: Other installations receive paths that do not exist for them, and the repository publishes a personal home path.

findings.observation: The Codex always-on template names one host ("On this Linux host") and gives two absolute home-directory paths of one machine for the ast-grep program and its configuration. The template is copied as the global instructions of every installation.
findings.consequence: Other installations receive paths that do not exist for them, and the repository publishes a personal home path.
findings.closure: The owner replaces the machine-specific lines with a portable instruction or a per-installation value, or records that the template is personal and not shipped.

findings.observation: The git-rails record (:29-90), including twenty residual-risk rows (:69-90), is appended to the always-on file delivered into every session. Workflows act on the Enforcement values of rules/git-flow.md:219-243; the risk table informs the owner and is cited only as the place where unseen commands are listed (rules/git-flow.md:249).
findings.consequence: Every session reads the full risk register although no workflow step acts on it.
findings.closure: The residual-risk register is delivered as reference context and the always-on part keeps the capability lines a workflow decides on.

findings.observation: Load-line detection marks spans on lines whose verb describes another reader, not a load: here :227 ("read it as not-started"), :247 and :311 ("read by /pe-finalize") and :282 ("read by orchestrators"); likewise rules/tdd.md:39, rules/run-log.md:86 and :582, rules/phase-atomic-execution.md:55 and rules/workflow-globals.md:36. Of the fourteen load edges in rule and adapter files only rules/workflow-globals.md:32 and :44 describe a load of the target, and :44 resolves to the wrong file (AUD-08-006).
findings.consequence: A load count taken from the detector overstates the loads of the rules, and the real bootstrap loads, written as table rows of `.ai/` paths, are not counted.
findings.closure: The textual load detection distinguishes a load instruction from a description of another reader, or the load inventory is taken from declared loads.

findings.observation: `## Context Pack` (:40) follows the last preamble line (:39) without a blank line and opens one section that runs to :127. Besides the optional pack it holds the global phase principles: never auto-advance (:56), continue never restart (:58), wait for user decisions (:60), the registry of workflow-declared mode overrides (:62-85), the `--batch` meaning (:87-94), the trust mechanism (:98-102), orchestrated mode (:106-112) and test-first execution (:114-120). The registry has no heading of its own although workflows/pav-propose.md:12 cites it as `workflow-globals → Workflow-declared mode overrides`.
findings.consequence: A section-level load or move of `## Context Pack` carries the core phase contract, a load of the principles without it is impossible, and the cited registry cannot be resolved as a section.
findings.closure: The principles stand under headings of their own (the mode-override registry among them) before any section-level loading or split of the file, and `## Context Pack` holds only the pack.

findings.observation: Besides the worked examples (AUD-08-010) the contract holds a decision protocol (`## The escalation gate`, :27-57: four conditions decide quick or full) and two procedures (`## Setting the flow (Discovery)`, :118-133, run by /pd-analyze; `## Mid-flight escalation (quick → full)`, :137-152, triggered by a breach).
findings.consequence: The target name `contract-quick-flow` will hold a protocol and two procedure sections.
findings.closure: The map keeps the gate and the procedures in the contract with a recorded reason, or splits them through an amendment.

findings.observation: Most of the section (:97-188) is the model-resolution protocol and the catalog guidance preflight procedure (:99-129); the table format itself is :190-203. Both apply only when a plan uses model columns or a model-specific request is made, but they load with every use of the state-file contract.
findings.consequence: Every workflow that loads the state-file reference reads the model-selection protocol even when no model column or request exists.
findings.closure: The model-resolution protocol and preflight are loaded only when model columns or a model-specific request are present, and the table format stays with the state-file contract.

findings.observation: Lines 2-3 are written as comments (a managed-file notice and a note on how the harness merges the file) but are Markdown level-1 headings; line 1 is the title.
findings.consequence: The always-on body delivered to every session carries two headings that are not headings.
findings.closure: The notices become prose or a comment form that Markdown does not read as a heading when the file moves to the Codex adapter.

findings.observation: Line 2 is written as a comment (the scope of the standards) but is a Markdown level-1 heading; line 1 is the title.
findings.consequence: The always-on body delivered to every session carries a heading that is not a heading.
findings.closure: The scope note becomes prose when the file moves to the Claude Code adapter.

findings.observation: Two references name `quick-flow → ## Mid-flight escalation (quick → full)`. The heading exists at rules/quick-flow.md:137, but its text contains the component separator ` → `, so the reference grammar splits it into `## Mid-flight escalation (quick` and `full)` and reports a missing heading. The references are correct on reading; the heading text makes them unresolvable by any grammar that splits on the separator. The same heading is cited unmarked at rules/workflow-globals.md:140.
findings.consequence: The naming migration's reference check reports these two pre-existing references as defects it must fix, and a renamed or moved escalation section would leave them stale without a reliable diagnostic.
findings.closure: The heading text no longer contains ` → ` (for example `(quick to full)`) and both references match it, or the migration's grammar resolves a component against a whole heading before splitting; both edges then resolve.

findings.observation: Four atomic workflows name `phase-atomic-execution → ## Context Bootstrap` for the runbook resolution with its umbrella fallback. The stem is both a rule and a workflow and both files have a `## Context Bootstrap` heading; on reading the rule is meant (rules/phase-atomic-execution.md:21-25). This is the pattern AUD-08-002 records in rules/phase-atomic-validation.md:21.
findings.consequence: A reader or tool cannot tell from the reference which file is meant; the shared stem resolves only through the surrounding prose.
findings.closure: Every reference names a stem that is unique after the naming migration (the rule's bootstrap name, the workflow `atomic-execution`).

findings.observation: Two section references omit the `##` marker of their target heading: `quick-flow → The quick path` (target `## The quick path — what changes`, rules/quick-flow.md:61) and `workflow-reference → Autonomous Subtask Classifier → Runtime self-correction` (targets rules/workflow-reference.md:487 and :530). Both targets exist, so a reader finds them, but the cross-reference syntax requires the marker and the migration's executable-reference grammar does not read the unmarked form.
findings.consequence: No grammar-based check or rewrite sees these references, so a renamed or split target leaves them stale without a diagnostic; the classifier section is a split target of the naming migration.
findings.closure: Both spans carry the markers of their target headings (`## The quick path — what changes`; `## Autonomous Subtask Classifier → ### Runtime self-correction (tripwire)`); the naming migration fixes them under AMD-08-01.

findings.observation: Both edges read `context-pack.md` inside the span `AI_DIR/context-pack.md`, which names the generated pack file in the project's knowledge base, not the workflow file `workflows/context-pack.md`. The token grammar matches the file name and resolves it to the workflow; on reading the references are correct. AUD-08-006 records the same resolution in rules/workflow-globals.md.
findings.consequence: None for the workflow; the edges count as suffixed workflow names only because the pack shares the workflow's stem.
findings.closure: No change; the observation stands while the pack keeps this file name.

findings.observation: Three lists map each child command to its workflow file name (`/pd-analyze` → `pd-analyze.md`). The file names are suffixed references outside the migration's grammar; `phase-atomic-execution.md` and `phase-atomic-validation.md` are also ambiguous between a rule and a workflow. The lists restate children that the phase orchestrators own, and line 109 forbids replaying them separately.
findings.consequence: The command renames of the naming migration leave every file name stale, and no grammar-based rewrite or check sees them.
findings.closure: The lists name commands only (`/<name>` without `.md`), or are removed in favour of the phase orchestrators; the naming migration fixes them under AMD-08-01.

findings.observation: The proposal semantics are cited as `workflow-globals → Workflow-declared mode overrides`, which is no heading: the registry sits inside `## Context Pack` (rules/workflow-globals.md:40, :62). This is the missing registry heading that AUD-08-026 records; this finding records the citing edge so the defect is not reported twice. Two active knowledge files cite the same non-heading: .ai/memory/architecture.md:164 and .ai/principles/architecture.md:41.
findings.consequence: The citation cannot be resolved or checked, and it points into a section whose heading says nothing about mode overrides.
findings.closure: The span names an existing heading in the marked form: the registry's own heading once AUD-08-026 gives it one, otherwise `## Context Pack`, whose extent holds the registry; the naming migration fixes this span and the two reader citations under AMD-08-01.

findings.observation: The workflow holds a contract: `## Recovery journal` defines the journal schema and the exact command forms that the git-rails hook verifies (restack.md:44-46, :90-93; rules/git-flow.md:205, :237). The rest of the file is the workflow's steps.
findings.consequence: The hook's evidence contract is read only through the workflow; a reader of the safety rails reaches the schema through a workflow body.
findings.closure: The section stays in place, since the validator pins the heading in this file (scripts/validate-contracts.sh:5636) and only this workflow writes the journal; context tiering records it as contract when it classifies the workflow.

findings.observation: Step 3 of `## Instructions` (lines 62-181) is the canonical ADR trigger, body template, numbering, file name and index schema. It is consumed by /adr-new (adr-new.md:11-13), /pd-design (pd-design.md:77), /spec-sync (spec-sync.md:101-102) and /bugfix (bugfix.md:138), and line 63 warns readers not to execute the other finalization steps while loading it.
findings.consequence: Every consumer loads the finalization section, and the contract has no heading of its own that a section reference can name.
findings.closure: The ADR schema is a section of its own (or a contract rule) that the four consumers cite by heading, and the finalization step cites it in turn.

findings.observation: Three orchestrators instruct to follow the `run-log` rule in full (phase-execution.md:18, phase-validation.md:19, spec-run.md:63); /bugfix follows the whole rule at :30. The rule has 585 lines, while a prompt-logged boundary needs `## Workflow coverage and routing` (rules/run-log.md:116), which /phase-discovery and /phase-pipeline cite as their only section (phase-discovery.md:135, phase-pipeline.md:19).
findings.consequence: Per workflow: /phase-execution and /phase-validation cite only the routing section (phase-execution.md:21, phase-validation.md:22) and /bugfix cites none, so each of their runs loads the native hook adapter, read-only lint and legacy normalization sections (rules/run-log.md:375, :523, :254) without using them. /spec-run does use the native hook adapter: it dispatches through the hook adapter (spec-run.md:286-301) and cites `### Dispatch and native evidence` (:331) besides routing (:80, :288, :335, :377), so for it only the read-only lint and legacy normalization sections go unused. AUD-08-013 records the rule side of the same cost.
findings.closure: /phase-execution, /phase-validation and /bugfix name the sections they use, as /phase-discovery does; /spec-run names its routing and dispatch sections instead of the whole rule; the rest loads only when the condition that needs it holds.

findings.observation: The tripwire loads the whole `workflow-reference` rule (634 lines) to use the Autonomous Subtask Classifier (rules/workflow-reference.md:487-548), at the start and again at the midpoint of every leaf. /pav-close (:32), /pe-finalize (:27) and /pv-finalize (:30) likewise load the whole rule for the status translation table, the memory entry format or the project-state update rules.
findings.consequence: Every leaf loads the state-file contract, the decision protocol and the model resolution protocol to evaluate one classifier section; AUD-08-018 and AUD-08-028 record the rule side.
findings.closure: Each of these workflows loads only the section it uses by its marked heading (`workflow-reference → ## Autonomous Subtask Classifier`, `## Status Translation Table`, `## .ai/memory/state.md Entry Format`, `## .ai/project_state.md Update Rules`).

findings.observation: Routine selection is offline (pd-select-model.md:15), yet every run loads the refresh procedure (:66-85) and the refresh candidate schema (:129-139), which apply only with `--refresh`, and the cost-comparison contract (:162-170), which applies only when the owner supplies qualified comparable-task evaluations.
findings.consequence: Each bulk or single selection loads instructions for paths it does not take.
findings.closure: The refresh procedure, the candidate schema and the cost-comparison contract load only under their conditions (a flag or a supplied evaluation).

findings.observation: The test level is reported before writing (:80-86), the criterion mapping before writing code (:133-139), and both again with the digest in the final report (:237-241). The final digest is suppressed only by `--batch` or /phase-pipeline, but /phase-atomic-execution calls /pae-tests without the flag (:101) and reports the level and RED result once more (:110-111); /spec-run asks the worker to report the RED digest after the step (:318, :325-326); /phase-pipeline asks for `--batch` (:47), but no workflow on its call chain passes it to /pae-tests.
findings.consequence: Each leaf reports the same level, mapping and digest up to three times in one session.
findings.closure: The level, mapping and digest are reported once per leaf at the boundary that needs them, and the callers that want suppression pass it on the actual call.

findings.observation: After Discovery completes, the pipeline reports the chosen approach (:116), which /pd-finalize already reported as the single final report that its parent reuses (pd-finalize.md:104-107; phase-discovery.md:178-179); the pipeline's final report restates the phase outcomes again (:153-156).
findings.consequence: The chosen approach is printed twice within one run and a third time in the final report.
findings.closure: The pipeline reuses /pd-finalize's report as a progress marker and adds only what it decides itself.

findings.observation: /phase-execution reports completed and skipped work, verification and paths and displays `Execution complete. Run /phase-validation <task-directory> to start validation.` (:100-101) right after /pe-finalize reported outcomes, verification and paths and displayed the same line (pe-finalize.md:106-107). /phase-validation repeats /pv-finalize's report the same way (phase-validation.md:105; pv-finalize.md:204-205), and /phase-atomic-validation reports the final verdict and status (phase-atomic-validation.md:85) right after /pav-close reported the closure and status (pav-close.md:70). /phase-discovery avoids this by letting /pd-finalize supply the single final report (phase-discovery.md:178).
findings.consequence: Every Execution and Validation phase, and every atomic validation cycle, ends with two reports of the same outcome.
findings.closure: The three orchestrators reuse their last child's report, as /phase-discovery does, and add only the run-closing facts they own.

findings.observation: Each leaf compresses the same parent state three times in one Execution: /pae-finalize after execution (pae-finalize.md:62), /pav-close after validation (pav-close.md:51) and /pe-execute right after the leaf is reviewed (:72). The /pav-close pass follows the writes of /pav-check, /pav-propose and its own status update; the /pe-execute pass follows no write since that pass. A composite check (phase-composite-validation.md:85), each fix cycle (pv-execute-fixes.md:43) and the orchestrated loop (spec-run.md:403) add further passes.
findings.consequence: Each pass reads the whole state and audits it against the protected-sections contract, so the cost grows with the number of leaves; the /pe-execute pass audits a state the /pav-close pass has just compressed, and the other two each follow only the few lines one step wrote.
findings.closure: One compression checkpoint per leaf cycle, owned by one workflow, with the others returning to it.

findings.observation: Proposals are recorded in `## Improvement Proposals (T-XX)` (:60-75) and their Do Later and Optional summaries are mirrored into the leaf's `notes:` (:77).
findings.consequence: The same record lives twice in one state file; /compress-state classifies such content as a duplicate to keep once (compress-state.md:25), so the mirror can be removed and later read from either place.
findings.closure: One location holds the proposals, and the leaf block points to it.

findings.observation: For a spec input, the pipeline runs `phase-discovery` Step 0 in full for resolution (:89-92), then runs /phase-discovery (:105), whose Step 0 parses the arguments, reads the spec, checks prefix collisions and locates task directories again (phase-discovery.md:58-93) on inputs nothing has changed in between. /spec-run does the same (spec-run.md:103-105, :134).
findings.consequence: Every pipeline and orchestrated run repeats the Discovery input checks once per start or resume.
findings.closure: The resolution-only result is passed to /phase-discovery, which skips the checks whose inputs are unchanged.

findings.observation: /pv-review reads the same task-owned file set that /pv-contract read immediately before (pv-contract.md:34-39), including the tests, and resolves the same `working_dir:` values; /phase-validation (:87-88) and /bugfix (:132) run the two steps back to back.
findings.consequence: Every Validation reads the unchanged implementation and test files twice; the two steps apply different criteria to the same inputs.
findings.closure: The second step reuses the file set and reading of the first in the same session, or the two reviews are one pass with two verdict sections.

findings.observation: After the fixes, three places order a recheck of contract and review: /pv-execute-fixes re-runs /pv-contract and /pv-review for the changed surface (:47), /phase-validation asks to recheck the affected contract and review findings before finalization (phase-validation.md:101-102), and /pv-finalize reruns both when the evidence does not cover the changed surface (pv-finalize.md:51-52).
findings.consequence: The orchestrator's recheck can run the two reviews again on code that has not changed since /pv-execute-fixes reviewed it.
findings.closure: One owner of the post-fix recheck; the others confirm its recorded evidence covers the changed surface.

findings.observation: Without sub-agents each critic round is a fresh pass that re-reads the spec and all Step 1 sources (:216-217), for up to ten rounds (:205). The Step 1 sources do not change between rounds, and the inline review is declared not independent anyway (:217-218).
findings.consequence: An inline loop re-reads unchanged project sources every round without gaining the independence the re-reading is meant to buy.
findings.closure: Inline rounds re-read only the changed spec and keep the Step 1 sources from the first round.

findings.observation: /pae-tests and /pae-implement load the `phase-atomic-execution` rule and "run the full bootstrap even when standalone" (pae-tests.md:56-58, pae-implement.md:53-55); /pae-finalize loads it again (:29-31). Under /phase-atomic-execution, which loaded it at :22, and inside one /spec-run worker that runs all three steps in the context it holds (spec-run.md:342-344), the rule is loaded three or four times per leaf. The rule itself reuses current sources (rules/phase-atomic-execution.md:10-14), so the repeat is the rule text and its bootstrap reports (:26, :28).
findings.consequence: Each atomic step reloads the rule and repeats the working-directory and loaded-file reports, and the workflow wording contradicts the rule's reuse clause.
findings.closure: The three steps load the rule only when no caller in the session has loaded it, as the rule's reuse clause states, and report the bootstrap once.

findings.observation: /pe-finalize runs the `phase-execution` Context Bootstrap "including standalone runs", that is under /phase-execution as well, which ran it at phase-execution.md:53. /pv-create-fixes (:29) and /pv-finalize (:29) do the same under /phase-validation (:54). Unlike the atomic phase rules, the phase-execution and phase-validation rules have no reuse clause (rules/phase-execution.md:10-12, rules/phase-validation.md:10-12). The global rules answer both ways: the standalone sentence says to run the full bootstrap and never assume pre-loaded context, while the next sentence reuses unchanged context within one parent invocation (rules/workflow-globals.md:35-36). Read literally, the step text reloads the seven bootstrap sources under its parent.
findings.consequence: Whether every Execution and Validation reloads the knowledge-base bootstrap inside the session that already holds it depends on which global sentence the agent applies; the step text, which says to bootstrap in both modes, points to the reload.
findings.closure: The three steps bootstrap only when invoked standalone, as /pe-execute does (pe-execute.md:23-24), or the two phase rules gain the reuse clause of the atomic rules.

findings.observation: Children load their phase rule unconditionally while limiting the full bootstrap to standalone runs (pe-execute.md:23-24, pav-check.md:24-25, pv-contract.md:22-23, pv-review.md:27-28, pv-execute-fixes.md:26-27), or run the bootstrap in both modes where the rule's reuse clause keeps the sources (pav-close.md:26, pav-propose.md:18, and phase-composite-validation.md:18 when /pav-close calls it). Their callers loaded the same rule (phase-execution.md:53, phase-atomic-validation.md:21, phase-validation.md:54, pav-close.md:26). The atomic-validation reuse clause keeps current sources for the same resolved project (rules/phase-atomic-validation.md:10-14), so a composite in another `working_dir:` loads its own sources legitimately; in every case the repeat is the rule text.
findings.consequence: The rule text is loaded again by each step of a phase; the general reuse rule (rules/workflow-globals.md:35-36) is not restated where the load is written.
findings.closure: The load sentence of each child is conditional on the rule not being loaded in the session.

findings.observation: /compress-state loads `workflow-reference → ## Protected Sections Contract` on every run, with no reuse condition. Its callers have already loaded the rule in the same session: /pd-finalize loads exactly that section (:25) before calling it (:75); /pe-finalize (:27), /pv-finalize (:30) and /pav-close (:32) load the whole rule; /pe-execute loads its model-resolution section (:42).
findings.consequence: Each compression, which runs several times per leaf (AUD-08-045), reloads part or all of a 634-line rule already in context.
findings.closure: The Guard loads the contract only when the caller has not loaded it in the session.

findings.observation: /bugfix loads the principles, architecture and state memory, ADR index and runbook in its Guard (:16-17) and later runs /pv-contract and /pv-review (:132). Neither runs under its parent orchestrator, so each performs the full `phase-validation` bootstrap (pv-contract.md:22-23, pv-review.md:27-28), whose rule has no reuse clause (rules/phase-validation.md:10-12); the standalone rule says never to assume pre-loaded context (rules/workflow-globals.md:35), while the next sentence reuses context within one parent invocation (:35-36).
findings.consequence: One defect fix loads the same seven sources three times, and the two global sentences give opposite answers for a non-orchestrator caller.
findings.closure: A caller that has loaded the bootstrap sources counts as the parent for reuse, and the two validation steps reuse them.

findings.observation: Within one Execution session `workflow-reference` is loaded at several call depths for every leaf: /pe-execute for model resolution (:41-42), /phase-atomic-execution for the same section (:76-77), /pae-implement twice for the classifier (pae-implement.md:125-126), /pae-finalize for the status translation table (:35), /pav-close for the same table (:32) and /compress-state for the protected sections (:12). These repeats lie two or three call levels apart, so no repeated-load candidate covers them.
findings.consequence: The 634-line rule is loaded several times per leaf; no workflow states that a load made earlier in the session is reused.
findings.closure: The rule, or the sections in use, is loaded once per session and reused by every deeper step while unchanged.

findings.observation: /pav-check loads the `tdd` rule for its audit (:55) after /pae-tests loaded `tdd → ## Test-level gate` (pae-tests.md:76) and /pae-implement enforced its GREEN section (pae-implement.md:107) for the same leaf. Under /pe-execute both subtrees run in one session (pe-execute.md:63-67), two call levels below it; /spec-run avoids the repeat with a separate Validator worker (spec-run.md:365-374).
findings.consequence: The 226-line rule is loaded twice per leaf in a non-orchestrated Execution.
findings.closure: The validation step reuses the rule loaded by the execution steps of the same session, or loads only the sections it audits.

findings.observation: The reference says /pv-classify-fixes is "called by fix creation in orchestrated mode", but /pv-create-fixes calls it in every mode before allocating fix-task IDs (pv-create-fixes.md:50-54), as /phase-validation states (:12, :90).
findings.consequence: A reader of the reference may skip classification outside /spec-run, and the fix IDs then lack the classification table that /pv-create-fixes reuses.
findings.closure: The reference row states that fix creation always calls the classifier.

findings.observation: /pae-tests and /pae-implement each report the resolved WORK_DIR before continuing (pae-tests.md:54, pae-implement.md:51) and then load the `phase-atomic-execution` rule, whose bootstrap reports `WORK_DIR=<path>, AI_DIR=<path>` again (rules/phase-atomic-execution.md:26) and lists the loaded files (:28). AUD-08-051 records the repeated load; this finding records the repeated report.
findings.consequence: Each of the two steps prints the same working-directory resolution twice, and a leaf cycle prints it four times.
findings.closure: The working directory is reported once per leaf, either by the step or by the rule bootstrap it loads.

findings.observation: The anchored line `Status values for atomic-execution / atomic-validation:` stands under `## Canonical Status Formats` (rules/workflow-globals.md:215) and again in rules/workflow-reference.md:226; the `atomic-tests` vocabulary follows both (:217 and :227) with the same values. The validator and the state-tool test read the vocabulary only from rules/workflow-globals.md (scripts/validate-contracts.sh:641, :2020; tests/state-tool.py:768), so the copy is read by no check.
findings.consequence: A change to the canonical vocabulary can leave the copy stale without a failing check, and readers of the state-file reference see two definitions.
findings.closure: rules/workflow-reference.md cites `workflow-globals → ## Canonical Status Formats` instead of restating the anchored lines, after the naming migration, which keeps every parent line starting `Status values for` (spec 09 AC-42).

findings.observation: Three workflows restate `workflow-reference → ### Model columns and resolution` (rules/workflow-reference.md:97-188) in about twenty lines each: workflows/phase-atomic-execution.md:76-98, workflows/pe-execute.md:41-62 and workflows/spec-run.md:181-205 (guidance preflight, helper call, identity display, fallback or stop, actual identity only from a receipt). The wording differs in each copy; read against the contract, none contradicts it. The caller-specific parts are short: /phase-atomic-execution reuses a caller's resolution only for the same invocation (:97-98), and /spec-run stops its setup when guidance is unavailable and never implements inline (:186, :203), the conservative path the contract leaves to its caller (rules/workflow-reference.md:124-125).
findings.consequence: A change to the contract has to be repeated in three paraphrases that no check compares, and each caller reads both the contract and its paraphrase (AUD-08-056).
findings.closure: Each workflow cites the contract and keeps only its caller-specific lines.

findings.observation: The text that moves into the atomic-execution bootstrap rule has 443 words by the migration's word count: the preamble (front matter and title, :1-7) 29, `## Context Bootstrap` (:8-43) 287 and `## Phase Behaviors` (:44-52) 127. The naming migration lets only `## Phase Behaviors` text overflow (spec 09 REQ-19), yet the preamble and `## Context Bootstrap` alone have 316 words; even with a one-word description, no title and only the citing line under `## Phase Behaviors` the rule would hold 302 words. The migration's own measurement at its parent snapshot (about 393 words, DM-10 → Overflow rules) predates the multi-repository runbook resolution at :21-25.
findings.consequence: The bootstrap target cannot satisfy the 300-word limit and its check (spec 09 REQ-19, REQ-32, AC-11) without deleting or rewording load instructions that the section map moves verbatim (DM-12).
findings.closure: The migration specification states how a bootstrap whose own context section exceeds the limit is delivered (AMD-08-03); nothing in the section is deleted.

amendments.current:
A finding this grammar produces on the parent tree is a pre-existing defect: the delivery
fixes it and lists it in DM-20 → Pre-existing reference defects.
amendments.proposed: A finding this grammar produces on the parent tree is a pre-existing defect: the delivery fixes it and lists it in DM-20 → Pre-existing reference defects. The same holds for every reference defect that 08's accepted report records with owner 09 outside this grammar, in scan set E or R: a section reference without its heading marker gains the marker of the existing heading; a reference to a paragraph label that is no heading names the heading whose extent holds the label; a reference broken across lines is joined into one span; a rule or workflow name with `.md` in a span loses the suffix or becomes a `/<name>` command. These fixes are edits permitted beside DM-1 substitutions; no `## ` heading is renamed or added for them, and each is listed in the same DM-20 table.
amendments.reason: The audit gives pre-existing reference defects to the naming migration (spec 08 A-18), but this grammar finds and fixes only marked section references, commands, rule names and paths in scan set E. The recorded defects outside it are unmarked or paragraph-label section references (AUD-08-001, AUD-08-004, AUD-08-005, AUD-08-033, AUD-08-036, AUD-08-062), a reference broken across lines (AUD-08-007) and suffixed workflow file names in span lists (AUD-08-035); REQ-25 renames their stems as stale names but neither repairs nor checks them, so they survive the migration unchecked.

amendments.proposed: AC-NN (DM-16, REQ-31) — Given the 08 report accepted by the owner and the delivered tree, then every reference that a 09-owned reference-defect finding of that report names outside the DM-16 grammar is a row of DM-20 → Pre-existing reference defects whose Fix cell names the applied fix, and the delivered text at that place is one span that names an existing heading with its marker and carries no `.md` after a rule or workflow name.
amendments.reason: AMD-08-01 adds an obligation that no acceptance criterion of the migration specification checks; without one the delivery can pass while the recorded defects remain.

amendments.current:
IF the moved text exceeds 300 words, THEN the excess `## Phase Behaviors`
  text SHALL move to the overflow rule DM-10 names for that phase, cited from
  `## Phase Behaviors`, and SHALL never be deleted.
amendments.proposed: IF the moved text exceeds 300 words, THEN the excess `## Phase Behaviors` text SHALL move to the overflow rule DM-10 names for that phase, cited from `## Phase Behaviors`, and SHALL never be deleted; IF the front matter, the moved `## Context Bootstrap` section and the citing line already exceed 300 words, THEN THE bootstrap rule SHALL keep that section whole, SHALL move all other `## Phase Behaviors` text to the overflow rule, and SHALL be listed with its measured word count and this reason in DM-20, and THE checker SHALL accept a listed rule over 300 words instead of reporting it (REQ-32).
amendments.reason: At the audited revision the atomic-execution bootstrap cannot meet the limit by overflow alone (AUD-08-063): its preamble and `## Context Bootstrap` already have 316 words, and DM-12 moves that section verbatim. Without a rule for this case the delivery either fails AC-11 or deletes or rewords load instructions, which REQ-19 forbids. Alternatives left to the owner: shorten the section under spec 11's obligation map before this migration, or move the path resolution that the atomic-validation bootstrap repeats (duplicate group DG-004) into a procedure rule; both change text that DM-12 moves verbatim.
